doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Move to Los Angeles, Duke and Louis
title: Film work and The Pawnbroker with Quincy Jones
summary: He never wanted to write for film and describes Quincy's focus.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Okay, before we take that on, as far as your educational career because I really want to focus on that and talk about not only your career… Burrell:…trajectory but also talk about how you’ve developed your curriculum and you pedagogy. I want to talk about, the reason why I asked about your career goals coming out to L.A. because this is, forgive me, Hollyweird, Hollywood. And you’ve already done the soundtrack of Pawnbroker with Quincy, that was done in the in the mid 60’s…
Right, that was in New York.
So I was just wondering if you had, you know, your sights set on getting into film, you know, doing film scores or T.V. or any of that.

No, I never thought about doing film scores, for some reason that was never interesting to me. No, I didn’t think about that. I wouldn’t mind playing on them, which I did, but as far as writing, no, I never thought about that.

What was that session like working on the Pawnbrokers? ‘Cause that was such a, I mean, that was a landmark movie and the soundtrack with Quincy. And of course he did In the Heat of the Night and others as well, In Cold Blood and those. But Pawnbrokers is what put him on the map.

Yeah, Quincy is a very focused guy, multitasking guy and extreme talent and knows what he wants. And that’s why to me he is so successful. Now he’s got a brilliant wealth of ideas and he knows how to make them, to put them in action. You know, his latest thing is We Are the World Two, you know, that’s unbelievable. But you know, his concept comes to him and he says, “Hey, I want to do this.” And so I’m not surprised at any success he has. It was exciting and fun, you know, working with him because you work with somebody who knows what they’re doing, knows what they want and is showing you by example, by there actions that this is what we’re doing and lets get to it with enthusiasm and it influences you. So that’s the kind of atmosphere, for me, always with Quincy at work, anyway. Socially he’s, you know, another laid back, well just laid back, but always thinking. He’s a great guy. But in a working situation its enthusiasm and focus, and knowing what the hell he’s doing, and he does, yeah.
